messages:
carmen: sharing a revised latency dashboard flow. Goals: reduce visual clutter, make sampling presets more discoverable, and improve accessibility for the heatmap. Prototype: https://figma.com/file/new-latency (view)

noah: looks promising. focusing on two things: 1) make the capture-rate presets explicit buttons under the timepicker, 2) compact the legend into a single-line pill with an overflow menu for additional metrics.

dina: thumbs up for presets. suggestion: label them with both percent and short intent: e.g., "Low — 5% (trend)", "Med — 20% (balanced)", "High — 80% (fidelity)". that helps non-technical users pick quickly.

ryan: UX nit: overflow menu should preserve keyboard order; when opened, first focus should land on the search field so users can type metric names quickly. also, the pill should show a count of active metrics (e.g., "3 metrics").

carmen: agreed on focus behavior. i'll change the pill to show active count and make the overflow a searchable list with checkboxes.

a11y-bot: accessibility checklist: 1) presets must be buttons with aria-pressed, 2) pill must have an accessible name like "Metrics selector (3 selected)", 3) heatmap cells need aria-label containing start-time, bin-size, metric, and value, 4) ensure colorblind-safe ramp + pattern fallback for low contrast areas.

noah: about the color ramp: current mock uses a teal->magenta ramp. can we test a blue->orange ramp and ensure it maps monotonically to value? also add a high-contrast toggle in the card menu.

dina: for low sample counts, propose a visible badge: a small outline tag in the top-right of the card that says "Low samples" when average samples/bin < threshold. make sure it's textual — not just color.

ryan: implementation: when presets change, we should debounce server calls (250ms) and show a small optimistic preview in the heatmap (fade) until real data arrives. avoids thrashing.

carmen: good call. I'll add an inline cost estimator next to presets that updates with the selected preset: "Est. tokens/day: 120k". keeps cost visible.

a11y-bot: cost estimator should be in a live region (aria-live=polite) so screen reader users hear updates when presets change. also ensure any inline toast messages announce properly.

dina: copy tweak for the preset helper: "Presets control the fraction of requests stored for analysis. Higher = better accuracy for tail metrics, higher cost." keep it short.

noah: legend pill behavior: clicking metric checkbox toggles visibility; shift-click toggles solo (turns others off). add an undo snackbar: "Show all metrics" with a 5s timeout.

ryan: performance: avoid re-rendering all heatmap DOM nodes on legend toggles. client-side masking + incremental updates. for huge windows, switch to aggregated tiles and show a small badge saying "aggregated" when bin size >1h.

a11y-bot: virtualized rendering allowed, but provide an alternate DOM list for screen readers summarizing hotspots (top 3 highest-value bins) to avoid blind navigation through thousands of cells.

carmen: question on p95 overlay: should p95 be a line on top of the heatmap or a separate sparkline above? mixed feelings. if we overlay, we need clear contrast and interaction affordances.

dina: preference: small sparkline above the heatmap that can be toggled to overlay. tooltip on hover shows p50/p90/p95/p99 and delta vs previous period.

noah: add small historical-context band: on hover of a p95 point, show faint band for p90-p99 and label it "903-99 range" (use accessible labeling).

a11y-bot: final notes: 1) ensure all interactive controls are reachable in a single tab sequence without hidden traps, 2) provide descriptive alt text for the card when included in dashboards exported as images, 3) confirm color tokens in spec (include hex + intended WCAG contrast ratios).

ops-bot: FYI: design assets scheduled to be published to staging components at 2026-04-05T09:00:00Z

carmen: great feedback. i'll update the Figma with preset labels, pill behavior, cost estimator, accessibility annotations, and the sparkline option. will post a handoff package (Figma + spec doc) here by EOD tomorrow and ping eng. thanks!
